  • Method Details

    • register

      public Queue<Optional<Identity>> register(@NonNull @NonNull Supplier<Optional<Identity>> Signal)
      Description copied from interface: Register
      Adds a signal to the collection of signals, these signals act as a source for associated numerical values which are provided back via a Queue, where the most recently provided element is the last element in the Queue.

      Note that this is done concurrently with updating Register.timestamp() Queues, so each update-cycle of Register.run() creates a pair of signal-values and timestamps that can be used to better interpolate values as opposed to a standard 20-millisecond cycle provided by Subsystem.periodic(), which provides lower accuracy.

      Specified by:
      register in interface Register<Supplier<Optional<Identity>>,Optional<Identity>>
      Parameters:
      Signal - Supplier of Numerical values which can be parsed as a double.
      Returns:
      Queue, should be retained and used to collect values periodically.
      See Also:
      • Figures.from(DoubleCircularBuffer)

    • timestamp

      public Queue<Double> timestamp()
      Description copied from interface: Register
      Creates a new Queue of standard size, and adds it to the collection of timestamp Queues. Each timestamp Queue contains the timestamp from a timestamp of a run-cycle, where the last element in the Queue is the most recent timestamp.

      Note that this is done concurrently with updating timestamp Queues, so each update-cycle of Register.run() creates a pair of signal-values and timestamps that can be used to better interpolate values as opposed to a standard 20-millisecond cycle provided by Subsystem.periodic(), which provides lower accuracy.

      Specified by:
      timestamp in interface Register<Supplier<Optional<Identity>>,Optional<Identity>>
      Returns:
      Queue, should be retained and used to collect values periodically.

    • start

      public void start()
      Description copied from interface: Register

      Makes a call to Register.run() and begins updating values appropriately. Ideally, calls to this method are only made once, but the method should contain logic to prevent multiple calls to Register.run() concurrently.

      However, this method should be capable of being used repeatedly with multiple calls to start and Register.halt()

      Specified by:
      start in interface Register<Supplier<Optional<Identity>>,Optional<Identity>>
      Overrides:

    • run

      public void run()
      Description copied from interface: Register

      Runs the main-loop of the underlying thread, updating Queues mapped to signals that have been registered, and updating Queues from the current system timestamp. Additionally, synchronization operations should occur to ensure multi-threading safety through the use of signal locks.

      Should only be called once via Register.start(), as the method contains an internal while-loop that continues as long as the Reporter is alive, and Closeable.close() has not yet been called.

      Specified by:
      run in interface Register<Supplier<Optional<Identity>>,Optional<Identity>>
      Specified by:
      run in interface Runnable
      Overrides:
